title: After a Hot Water Installation: Your Handover and Recordkeeping Checklist
metaTitle: Hot Water Installation Handover Checklist | Grade A Plumbing
metaDescription: Know what to keep after a hot water installation: model records, user instructions, warranty details, service contacts and questions for your installer.
author: Grade A Plumbing
excerpt: A practical checklist for understanding your new hot water system and keeping the records you may need for maintenance or a future fault.

sections.heading: Make the handover about your installed system
paragraphs: A hot water installation is not fully understood just because warm water reaches a tap. Before the installer leaves, ask for a plain-language handover that identifies the equipment, explains the user instructions and tells you who to contact if something changes. This guide is a recordkeeping aid, not an installation standard or a substitute for the manufacturer's manual. It does not tell you to open covers, adjust internal settings or test safety components. The goal is to leave you with useful information rather than a collection of documents you cannot connect to the actual installation.

Start with the exact system description. Australian Government guidance distinguishes storage and instantaneous water heating, and explains electric, gas, solar and heat pump arrangements. Ask the installer which description fits your installation and whether any separate tank, booster or controller belongs to it. Record the brand and model rather than relying on a sales description such as efficient hot water. If several components have their own manuals, keep those together. A photo of an accessible label can be useful, but there is no reason to move equipment or remove a panel to obtain one.

Write a short handover note in your own words: which part provides hot water, which document covers ordinary user operation, and which contact handles service enquiries. If you are uncertain about a term, ask for an explanation while the equipment is being discussed. Tell the installer if another household member will manage the system, or if the property will be rented out. Request information that can be passed on without someone needing to repeat the whole conversation. Practical questions are more valuable than guessing what an unfamiliar indicator or setting means.

sections.heading: Keep identification and purchase records together
paragraphs: Create one digital folder or envelope for the installation. Include the accepted scope, final invoice, model details, relevant user manuals and any documents actually supplied by the installer. Record the completion date separately from any manufacturing date shown on a label. Those dates answer different questions. Keep photographs of the installed equipment taken from a safe, accessible position. Do not assume every installation has the same paperwork: ask the installer what applies to the work completed, and seek the relevant regulator's current guidance if you need to confirm a documentation requirement.

Name files so that a future household member can find them. A useful filename identifies the property, equipment and document type without including unnecessary personal information. For example, separate the invoice from the user manual and any warranty registration acknowledgement. If a document arrives later, add it to the same folder rather than leaving it in an unrelated email thread. Keep an offline copy if you depend on email access. A tidy record is especially helpful when ownership, property management or the person responsible for maintenance changes.

If the agreed work changed during installation, ask for a written explanation of the final scope. Your own note should distinguish what was installed from what was discussed but not included. Avoid presenting a suggested future upgrade as completed work. Equally, do not treat an estimate of running costs as a measured result for your household. These small distinctions make later enquiries more precise. They also prevent a future service provider from drawing conclusions from an old proposal that does not accurately describe the equipment now in place.

sections.heading: Ask where the user instructions end
paragraphs: Ask the installer to identify the section of the manufacturer's manual that is intended for the household user. This is different from an installation or service manual. Confirm which visible controls, if any, you are expected to use and which functions should be left to a professional. Do not experiment with internal controls to see what happens. If a display shows an unfamiliar message, record the message as it appears and consult the user instructions or the nominated service contact. A general internet explanation for another model is not a reliable replacement for your own instructions.

For a system with a timer or app, ask what the supplied settings mean and whether the arrangement has been explained for your household. Do not assume that every electric system should run on the same schedule. YourHome discusses controlling electric water heating and the differences between system types, but a suitable arrangement still needs to match the equipment and installation. Keep a note of the explanation you receive, including any ordinary user steps demonstrated. If you subsequently change an allowed user setting, write down the change so a later enquiry has an accurate history.

Treat the handover as a chance to establish boundaries, not as a lesson in do-it-yourself servicing. Ask what visible changes should prompt a service enquiry and where to find the manufacturer's advice. If the installer describes a condition as normal, request a model-specific explanation rather than extending that answer to other equipment. Never ignore an active leak, electrical concern or suspected gas emergency because a checklist says the system was recently installed. A recordkeeping guide cannot assess safety remotely, and a new installation date does not establish that a later symptom is harmless.

sections.heading: Clarify service and warranty contacts
paragraphs: Ask who you should contact for a performance question, a suspected fault and a paperwork question. Those may be different contacts. Save the installer and manufacturer details with the model record, and use the contact information supplied through official documents rather than a number from an unrelated advertisement. If warranty registration is required under the product's terms, ask who is responsible for it and how completion will be confirmed. This guide does not interpret your warranty or promise that any particular fault will be covered; the applicable documents and circumstances need to be considered.

Read the warranty documents before assuming that product cover, labour, call-out costs and installation workmanship are all treated identically. Write down any questions and request clarification from the appropriate provider. Avoid reducing a warranty to a single number of years. A product description may refer to one component rather than every part of the installation. Keep the actual terms, proof of purchase and correspondence. If a problem occurs, those records help explain what you bought and what was agreed, even where the person initially answering your enquiry was not involved in the installation.

Ask where the recommended service information is documented and who can perform any required work. Record reminders using the guidance for the installed model, not a generic schedule copied from another product. Do not undertake a service procedure merely because it appears in a technical manual. YourHome describes different system configurations, including arrangements with separate components, so keeping the matching instructions matters. If someone gives you a verbal recommendation, ask whether it is a manufacturer requirement, an installation-specific recommendation or optional advice. That distinction helps you organise maintenance without turning every suggestion into an assumed obligation.

sections.heading: Build a useful history without trying to diagnose faults
paragraphs: Keep a simple log if you notice a change after installation: the date, what happened, which outlets were affected and any message shown on the user display. Describe observations rather than assigning a cause. For example, saying that a shower turned cold during use is more useful than asserting that a particular internal component failed. Include changes to permitted user settings and any previous service visit. Do not repeat a fault deliberately, expose yourself to unsafe conditions or dismantle equipment to gather evidence. Contact an appropriate professional when a symptom needs assessment.

If you are evaluating energy use, keep actual bills and note changes in household occupancy or habits. A bill comparison on its own does not prove the system's individual consumption, because tariffs and other household loads can change. Ask how any quoted estimate was calculated and what it includes. Avoid promising savings to another owner or tenant based on your first bill. The government sources explain broad technology choices, not a guaranteed financial result for your property. A careful record separates the product you installed, expectations discussed before purchase and what you subsequently observed.

For Melbourne households seeking a hot water assessment or planning a replacement, contact Grade A Plumbing on (02) 5837 5457 or email support@gradeaplumbing.store. Explain the model, the question you need answered and whether you have the installation records. Confirm current availability and the scope of any proposed visit before booking. General information in this article does not establish suitability for an individual property, a response time or a quoted price. Keep the handover folder accessible: its purpose is to make the next conversation clearer, not to replace a qualified assessment when one is needed.

faq.question: Does this checklist replace an installer handover?
faq.answer: No. Use it to organise questions and records. The installer and the manufacturer's instructions must explain the equipment actually installed at your property.

faq.question: Should I adjust internal settings after installation?
faq.answer: Do not open covers or adjust internal controls. Ask which ordinary user functions apply to your model and follow its user instructions.

faq.question: What should I send with a service enquiry?
faq.answer: The accessible model details, installation date, observed symptom and relevant service history. Do not take risks or dismantle equipment to collect information.
